title: Residue fields of Spec R and the canonical morphism Spec kappa(p) -> Spec R
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. Let $\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)$ be the residue field of the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-residue-field] and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. There is a ring isomorphism $e:\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (induced by $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak p}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$) such that $e^{-1}\circ\pi$ is the composite $R=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak p}\to\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)$ (germ followed by residue map), and such that the canonical morphism $j_{\mathfrak p}:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ (Spec of the residue map followed by $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak p}\to\operatorname{Spec}R$) equals $\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)$, i.e. $j_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1}\circ\pi)$.
